description: Students conduct a contemporary examination of race and racism, specifically anti-Black racism, in the United States through the lens of economics. This examination incorporates economic scholarship on the causes and persistence of racism beyond neoclassical economic theories of discrimination. Using economic research, students learn the ways in which race has been constructed, explore the inequalities in economic outcomes by race, and study how racist practices and institutions contribute to them. Offered annually during spring semester. Prerequisite: ECON 121 Principles of Economics or permission of the instructor.
name: Political Economy of Race & Racism
prerequisites: ECON 121 Principles of Economics or permission of the instructor.
